statements.rule: Writes the value of `e` to `name`, a field of the record or a local. `e` must have `name`'s type, an `i64` widens to an `f64`, and `null` fits any type. Writing `null` to a field removes it.
Gives `name` the type `T` and writes `e`. This also converts the type declaration to `T`.
Declares the type of `name` in advance. Use before parse functions to coerce types and improve performance.
Binds a local variable scoped to this block. It never reaches the record, and it takes the type of `e`. `let name: T = e;` gives it a type.
Replaces the whole record with the [object](#objects) `e`.
Writes each field of the object `e` into the object `o`, converting each value to the type of its field in `o`. `Object.assign($, e)` writes into the record.
Runs the first block where `c` is true, and the `else` block where it is false or null. `else if` chains.
Compares `e` with each `case` value, in order, with `==`. Runs from the first that matches through every case after it, until a `break`. `default` matches when no case does, and comes last.
Runs the block once per element of the array `a`, with `x` that element.

Runs the block while `c` is true. The code step has a time budget, 100 ms by default and configured by `SMELTR_LOOP_BUDGET_MS`, to prevent infinite loop stalls. When it runs out, a loop still running stops and marks each record whose condition is still true with a `LoopBudgetExceeded` exception.
Leaves the innermost loop or `switch`.
Ends this trip of the innermost loop and starts the next.
A local function. A parameter or result with no type takes its value's type. The body's last expression, written without a semicolon, is its value.
Ends the function with the value `e`.

Runs the block until a record's first exception that loses a value. The write that failed keeps the name's old value. A `catch` then runs on that record, with the exception cleared; `e.kind` is its kind and `e.message` its text. `finally` runs on every record that entered the `try`. A `try` needs a `catch`, a `finally` or both.
Runs on the records holding one of the kinds it names, and clears only those. Several catches are tried in order; a catch with no type takes every kind left, and comes last.
In a `catch`, puts the caught exception back on the record, for an outer `try` or its exception answer.
Removes each named field from the record. A field bound outside an `if`, loop or `try` cannot be deleted inside one; write `a = null` there.
Renames the field `from` to `to`, and removes `from`.
Discards the record.

Replaces the record with one record per element of the array field `a`, each holding its element at `a`. `unroll(a, true)` keeps the record's other fields on each. It stands outside every `if`, loop and `try`.

parseFunctions.name: json
parseFunctions.summary: The object the JSON `text` holds. It reads lenient JSON too, such as a trailing comma, raw control characters and `\xHH` escapes.

options.name: splitDots
options.holds: Whether a key holding dots is split into a nested path: `a.b` becomes `{a: {b}}`.

options.name: formats
options.holds: The text format of each `datetime` field, by name: `{ts: "%d/%m/%Y"}`. The specifiers are `parseTime`'s.

parseFunctions.name: kv
parseFunctions.signature: kv(text, {pairSep, kvSep, quote, escapes, nextKey, skip, splitDots, formats})
parseFunctions.summary: An object of the `key=value` pairs in `text`. Every value is a `str`.

options.name: pairSep
options.holds: The character between one pair and the next.

options.name: kvSep
options.holds: The character between a key and its value.

options.name: quote
options.holds: The character around a value that holds `pairSep`; `null` for none.

options.name: escapes
options.holds: Whether a backslash escapes any character in any value, quoted or not: `\n`, `\r` and `\t` are control characters and any other `\x` is `x`. Without it, only `\"` and `\\` inside quotes are escapes.

options.name: nextKey
options.holds: Whether an unquoted value runs to the `pairSep` before the next key: in `level=info debug x=1`, `level` is `info debug`. Off, a value ends at the first `pairSep` and `debug` is a bare key, `debug=true`.

options.name: skip
options.holds: Keys that make no field.

options.name: splitDots
options.holds: Whether a key holding dots is split into a nested path: `a.b` becomes `{a: {b}}`.

options.name: formats
options.holds: The text format of each `datetime` field, by name: `{ts: "%d/%m/%Y"}`. The specifiers are `parseTime`'s.

parseFunctions.name: cef
parseFunctions.summary: An object of the ArcSight CEF record in `text`: the seven header fields as `version`, `deviceVendor`, `deviceProduct`, `deviceVersion`, `deviceEventClassId`, `name` and `severity`, and each extension key as written. Text before `CEF:` is skipped. Every value is a `str`.

options.name: splitDots
options.holds: Whether a key holding dots is split into a nested path: `a.b` becomes `{a: {b}}`.

options.name: formats
options.holds: The text format of each `datetime` field, by name: `{rt: "%b %d %Y %H:%M:%S"}`. The specifiers are `parseTime`'s.

parseFunctions.name: csv
parseFunctions.signature: csv(text, [headers], {delimiter, quote, escape, squeeze, trim, splitDots, formats})
parseFunctions.summary: An object of one CSV line's columns, named by `headers` in order. A `null` header skips its column. Every value is a `str`.

options.name: delimiter
options.holds: The character between columns.

options.name: quote
options.holds: The character that quotes a column, which may then hold the delimiter.

options.name: escape
options.holds: The character that escapes a quote, or itself, inside a quoted column. `null` reads a doubled quote as one.

options.name: squeeze
options.holds: Whether a run of delimiters is one, as aligned columns write.

options.name: trim
options.holds: Whether spaces around each unquoted column are dropped.

options.name: splitDots
options.holds: Whether a key holding dots is split into a nested path: `a.b` becomes `{a: {b}}`.

options.name: formats
options.holds: The text format of each `datetime` field, by name: `{ts: "%d/%m/%Y"}`. The specifiers are `parseTime`'s.

parseFunctions.name: grok
parseFunctions.summary: An object of the fields the first matching pattern captures. Each `%{NAME:field}` captures `field`. Every value is a `str`.

options.name: patterns
options.holds: Your own patterns by name, `{NAME: "regex"}`, which the patterns may use as `%{NAME}`.

options.name: splitDots
options.holds: Whether a key holding dots is split into a nested path: `a.b` becomes `{a: {b}}`.

options.name: formats
options.holds: The text format of each `datetime` field, by name: `{ts: "%d/%m/%Y"}`. The specifiers are `parseTime`'s.

parseFunctions.name: lookup
parseFunctions.signature: lookup(table, key, {match, column, first, all, fields, formats})
parseFunctions.summary: An object of the `fields` read from the row of the lookup table `table` that `key` matches. A field with no match and no default is left out.

options.name: match
options.holds: How `key` matches the key column: `"exact"`, `"cidr"` or `"regex"`.

options.name: column
options.holds: The key column. A MaxMind database has none.
options.default: required, except for a MaxMind database

options.name: first
options.holds: `true`: the first matching row, in table order.

options.name: all
options.holds: `true`: every matching row; each field is an array.

options.name: fields
options.holds: Each output named for its column, `"column"`, or for its column and its default, `["column", "default"]`.

options.name: formats
options.holds: The text format of each `datetime` field, by name: `{ts: "%d/%m/%Y"}`. The specifiers are `parseTime`'s.
